description: Average over only the order items that have invoice line items.

b.request: Restrict to order items with at least one invoice line item (inner join). For each, average `derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost` over its non-NULL ratios and count its invoice line items. Then return the average of those per-item ratios and the average count across those items, in one row.
b.sql: WITH item_stats AS (SELECT oi.order_item_id, AVG(CAST(ili.derived_product_cost AS REAL) / ili.derived_total_cost) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_count FROM Order_Items oi INNER JOIN Invoice_Line_Items ili ON ili.order_item_id = oi.order_item_id GROUP BY oi.order_item_id) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio, AVG(line_count) AS avg_line_count FROM item_stats;
b.raw: Restrict to order items with at least one invoice line item (inner join). For each, average `derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost` over its non-NULL ratios and count its invoice line items. Then return the average of those per-item ratios and the average count across those items, in one row.

c.request: Per order item, work out the average of `derived_product_cost` ÷ `derived_total_cost` over its invoice line items (skipping missing ratios) and how many invoice line items it has. In a single row, what are the overall average of those per-item ratios (ignoring missing ones) and the average number of invoice line items per order item? Average over only the order items that have invoice line items.
c.sql: WITH per_item AS (SELECT order_item_id, AVG(CASE WHEN derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL AND derived_total_cost <> 0 THEN derived_product_cost * 1.0 / derived_total_cost END) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY order_item_id) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_avg_ratio, AVG(line_count) AS avg_line_items_per_order_item FROM per_item;

d.request: Per order item that has at least one invoice line item, compute AVG(derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost) over its Invoice_Line_Items rows (excluding NULL ratios) and COUNT of its Invoice_Line_Items rows; then return in one row the AVG of those per-item ratio averages (ignoring NULLs) and the AVG of the per-item invoice line item counts, restricted to order items with invoice line items.
d.sql: WITH item_stats AS (SELECT order_item_id, AVG(derived_product_cost * 1.0 / derived_total_cost) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY order_item_id) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_item_avg_ratios, AVG(line_count) AS avg_invoice_line_item_count FROM item_stats;

a.request: For each order item that appears in the invoice line items, take the average of `derived_product_cost` divided by `derived_total_cost` across its invoice line items (skipping missing ratios), and count its invoice line items. Then return one row with the average of those per-item average ratios (ignoring missing ones) and the average of those per-item line-item counts.
a.sql: SELECT AVG(item_avg_ratio) AS avg_of_item_avg_ratios, AVG(line_item_count) AS avg_of_item_line_item_counts FROM (SELECT order_item_id, AVG(CAST(derived_product_cost AS REAL) / derived_total_cost) AS item_avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items GROUP BY order_item_id);
